[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"PL/SQL Basics (Blocks, Variables, Control Structures)"},{"order":2,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction to PL/SQL"},{"order":3,"type":"paragraph","text":"PL/SQL (Procedural Language/SQL) is Oracle's procedural extension to SQL. It combines the data manipulating power of SQL with the processing power of procedural languages. PL/SQL allows you to write stored procedures, functions, and triggers, enhancing the capabilities of your database applications."},{"order":4,"type":"subheading","text":"PL/SQL Blocks"},{"order":5,"type":"paragraph","text":"A PL/SQL block is the fundamental unit of a PL/SQL program. It consists of three sections: DECLARE, BEGIN, and EXCEPTION. Only the BEGIN section is mandatory."},{"order":6,"type":"code","text":"DECLARE
  -- Declaration section (optional)
  variable_name data_type;
BEGIN
  -- Execution section (mandatory)
  -- SQL and PL/SQL statements
EXCEPTION
  -- Exception handling section (optional)
  WHEN exception_name THEN
    -- Handle the exception
END;"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"The DECLARE section is used to define variables, constants, and cursors. The BEGIN section contains the executable statements. The EXCEPTION section handles errors that may occur during execution."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Variables in PL/SQL"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Variables in PL/SQL must be declared before they can be used. The declaration specifies the variable's name and data type."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"variable_name data_type [:= initial_value];"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Example:"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"DECLARE
  v_employee_id NUMBER(6);
  v_employee_name VARCHAR2(50) := 'John Doe';
  v_salary NUMBER(8,2) := 5000.00;
BEGIN
  -- Your code here
  NULL;
END;"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Common Data Types: NUMBER, VARCHAR2, DATE, BOOLEAN"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Control Structures"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"PL/SQL provides several control structures to control the flow of execution, including conditional statements (IF-THEN-ELSE) and loops (FOR, WHILE)."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Conditional Statements (IF-THEN-ELSE)"},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"IF condition THEN
  -- Statements to execute if the condition is true
ELSIF condition THEN
  -- Statements to execute if the condition is true
ELSE
  -- Statements to execute if none of the conditions are true
END IF;"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Example:"},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"DECLARE
  v_age NUMBER := 25;
BEGIN
  IF v_age >= 18 THEN
    DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE('Eligible to vote');
  ELSE
    DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE('Not eligible to vote');
  END IF;
END;"},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Loops"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"PL/SQL supports FOR loops and WHILE loops."},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"FOR Loop"},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"FOR counter IN [REVERSE] lower_bound .. upper_bound LOOP
  -- Statements to execute
END LOOP;"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"Example:"},{"order":25,"type":"code","text":"BEGIN
  FOR i IN 1..5 LOOP
    DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE('Iteration: ' || i);
  END LOOP;
END;"},{"order":26,"type":"subheading","text":"WHILE Loop"},{"order":27,"type":"code","text":"WHILE condition LOOP
  -- Statements to execute
END LOOP;"},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"Example:"},{"order":29,"type":"code","text":"DECLARE
  v_counter NUMBER := 1;
BEGIN
  WHILE v_counter <= 5 LOOP
    DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE('Counter: ' || v_counter);
    v_counter := v_counter + 1;
  END LOOP;
END;"},{"order":30,"type":"subheading","text":"Exception Handling"},{"order":31,"type":"paragraph","text":"Exception handling allows you to gracefully handle errors that occur during the execution of your PL/SQL code."},{"order":32,"type":"code","text":"DECLARE
  -- Declarations
BEGIN
  -- Executable statements
EXCEPTION
  WHEN exception_name THEN
    -- Handle the exception
  WHEN OTHERS THEN
    -- Handle any other exception
END;"},{"order":33,"type":"paragraph","text":"Example:"},{"order":34,"type":"code","text":"DECLARE
  v_number NUMBER := 0;
BEGIN
  v_number := 10 / 0;
EXCEPTION
  WHEN ZERO_DIVIDE THEN
    DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE('Cannot divide by zero!');
  WHEN OTHERS THEN
    DBMS_OUTPUT.PUT_LINE('An unexpected error occurred.');
END;"},{"order":35,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":36,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial covered the basics of PL/SQL, including blocks, variables, control structures, and exception handling. Mastering these concepts is crucial for developing robust and efficient database applications in Oracle."}]
